newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tobacco talks stalled a week - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tobacco talks stalled a week - paper.

text.p: Tobacco-settlement talks may have been put off for at least a week amid an internal dispute over whether to give the tobacco industry full immunity from punitive damages, according to the Wall Street Journal.
In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said that despite the battle over the issue, the talks were likely to resume in a week's time.
The New York Times reported in its Monday edition that the widening rift over the liability issue may lead to a settlement proposal even if all of the states involved in the talks do not concur.
About 30 states are suing cigarette companies to recover Medicaid money spent on smoking-related illnesses.

"If a substantial majority of states agree to go forward, I think there will be a deal announced among the states who agree to it," Richard Scruggs, a lawyer who represents Mississippi and some 19 other states involved in the talks, told the Times. "Right now, the tail is wagging the dog."
Among the issues in dispute are whether a prohibition on punitive damages should be imposed and restrictions on the right of future smokers to sue.
